sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties at Bar.
Perused the material available on record.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner, who is aged about 19 years and 6 months, old has been falsely implicated in the present case.
Learned counsel submitted that as per the prosecution, the petitioner was pressurizing the victim- 'P', who is aged about 18 years, to marry him.

As per the prosecution, the petitioner on 04.06.2023 subjected victim- 'P' to forcible sexual assault and also captured obscene videos and [2025:RJ-JD:1841] (2 of 4) [CRLMB-16053/2024]
photographs of hers.
The petitioner thereafter, started threatening her to viral obscene videos and photographs of her if she would not agree to marry him.

Learned counsel submitted that the further prosecution story is that on 05.08.2024, the petitioner called the victim- 'P' behind the government school situated in the village and forcibly made her to drink poison.
The petitioner also consumed poison.
When after consuming poison their health condition started deteriorating, the victim- 'P' went to her house from where she was taken to the hospital.
The petitioner was also taken to the hospital by her family members.

Drawing attention of the Court towards the challan papers, learned counsel submitted that during the course of investigation, the Investigating Agency has not recovered any obscene videos and photographs of the victim- 'P' allegedly captured by the petitioner on 04.06.2023.
There is not even an iota of evidence available on record that the petitioner had any motive or intention to kill the victim- 'P'.
It was contended that as a matter of fact, the petitioner and the victim- 'P' were having an affair and wanted to marry.
However, their family members were not happy with their relationship.
In these circumstances, they decided to end their lives by consuming poison.
The allegation against the present petitioner that he forced/ made victim- 'P' to consume poison
is absolutely baseless and without any substance.

Lastly, learned counsel submitted that the petitioner is in judicial custody, the petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents; and the trial against the petitioner is not likely to [2025:RJ-JD:1841]
(3 of 4) [CRLMB-16053/2024] concluded in the near future and therefore, he may be enlarged on bail.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor as well as learned counsel for the complainant have vehemently opposed the bail application.

Having perused the FIR and the challan papers, this Court prima facie finds that the petitioner, who is aged about 19 years and 6 months, is in judicial custody; the investigation against the petitioner has already been concluded; no obscene videos and photographs of the victim- 'P' have been recovered from the possession of the present petitioner.

After scanning the material available on record, this Court is of the prima facie opinion that the question as to whether the petitioner had forced the victim- 'P' to consume poison or this is a case wherein petitioner and victim- 'P' were having an affair and wanted to marry but looking to the objection of their family members, they decided to commit suicide by consuming poison is a question to be decided by the competent criminal Court on the basis of the evidence and material produced before it by the Investigating Agency.

This Court observes that the present petitioner does not have any criminal antecedents and the fact that he himself consumed poison with an intention to commit suicide on the date of the alleged incident, cannot be overlooked at this stage.

Therefore, this Court is of opinion that it will not be prudent at this stage to keep the petitioner behind the Bars for an indefinite period by rejecting this bail application particularly when the investigation in the matter has already been concluded and the prosecution has not shown any apprehension of the petitioner influencing the victim- 'P' or other material [2025:RJ-JD:1841] (4 of 4) [CRLMB-16053/2024] prosecution witnesses of the case or fleeing away from justice in case, he is enlarged on bail.

Thus, without expressing any opinion on merits/demerits of the case, this Court is inclined to enlarge the Vikas vs State Of Rajasthan (2025:Rj-Jd:1841) on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102004571/
2 petitioner on bail.
Consequently, the bail application under Section 483 BNSS is allowed.

It is ordered that the accused-petitioner Vikas S/o Late Gangaram arrested in connection with F.I.R. No.138/2024,
registered at Police Station Bhaleri, Dist. Churu, shall be released on bail, if not wanted in any other case, provided he furnishes a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each, to the satisfaction of learned trial court, for his appearance before that court on each & every date of hearing and whenever called upon to do so till completion of the trial.
It is however, made clear that findings recorded/observations made above are for limited purposes of adjudication of bail application.
The trial court shall not get prejudiced by the same.

(KULDEEP MATHUR),J 94-himanshu/-
